source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"The symptoms are a pseudo-relapse because any new neurologic symptom lasting more than 24 hours is caused by heat or infection.","B":"The symptoms are routine daily fluctuation and do not require assessment when they persist for two days.","C":"The findings may represent an MS relapse and warrant evaluation, including assessment for infection, fever, heat, or another pseudo-relapse trigger.","D":"The symptoms establish permanent disease progression because an MS relapse cannot cause new visual or sensory findings."}}
source_row.rationale: A true MS relapse is characterized by new or worsening neurologic symptoms lasting more than 24 hours and not explained by infection, fever, or another pseudo-relapse trigger. New persistent visual and sensory symptoms therefore warrant prompt assessment by the MS care team.
source_row.source_detail: Definition of MS relapse and recommendation to contact the MS provider for new or worsening symptoms lasting more than 24 hours Source has no separate formal version identifier in the cited page metadata; live currentness and applicability rechecked 2026-08-15. source_row.stem: A client with multiple sclerosis develops new visual disturbance and numbness that persist for two days. What is the nurse's best interpretation?
